_about: Evidence for the rubric items that need a phone or a hand check (docs/tracking-rubric.md, `phone` and `manual` tags). npm run rubric reads this file. Set status to pass or fail, add the date and a note naming the recording or the measurement. docs/phone-session.md says what to record.

R1.03.note: Needs recordings/<date>/ with at least 200 labelled taps (range mode) and `node scripts/validate.mjs recordings/<date>` exiting 0; the scorer reads the folder itself, this entry is informational.

R2.09.note: Bench (?bench, Sample person or a photo of a player, drift run) on the slowest phone at 3 m: lock on target above 90% of frames.

R3.09.note: Recording backlight-3m__<phone>__1.json: target in front of a window, 20 range-mode taps, wrong 0.

R3.10.note: Recording partial-back-1.5m__<phone>__1.json: 10 back-view taps with the legs out of frame, wrong 0.

R3.11.note: After 5 minutes of play, the shot log's live samples all belong to the right player (compare via and the top-two similarities).

R3.12.note: Debug overlay on, pan across the whole group for 30 s: names and confidence agree with who is there.

R4.06.note: From the shot log of a real round: share of hits whose LOCK label was already green at the tap, target 80%.

R4.07.note: 10-minute round: UNCLEAR TARGET on a clearly aimed face-on 3 m shot fewer than 1 in 10 (shot log).

R4.09.note: Shot log timestamps on the fastest phone: median tap-to-verdict under 400 ms.

R5.01.note: Range test (debug, range, target and distance, 20 taps per cell) at 1.5/3/4.5/6/8 m face-on and back view: wrong 0 in every cell. Recordings stationary-<d>m__<phone>__<n>.json.

R5.02.note: Same table: every cell meets the target in docs/tracking-rubric.md section 5 on the players' phones in the venue light.

R5.03.note: Same table with half the lights off: within 15 points of the good-light numbers.

R6.12.note: Bench period with 2 enrolled profiles vs 12 on the slowest phone; the period must not grow with player count.

R6.13.note: Six or more players in one camera frame: frame period stays under 2x the single-body period (bench line or debug FPS).

R6.14.note: outfitConflict over all 66 pairs of 12 synthetic 51-bin outfits: 66 pairs in 0.64 ms in Node on the Mac; the lobby lists every conflicting pair (Lobby.tsx conflicts loop), verified by the e2e lobby-gating scenario naming the pair.

R6.17.note: e2e lobby-gating: a player joined and enrolled after the host had enrolled; the host stayed enrolled and Start enabled once the newcomer's outfit was distinct.

R6.18.note: Not built: a round timer or a last-two-standing call-out. Nice-to-have.

R7.01.note: One phone of each kind (iOS Safari, Android Chrome): guest enrolment end to end (8 head angles, front and back body scans, far-face step, outfit check) without a dead end.

R7.03.note: Mid-round: take a call, lock the screen, switch apps; back in the same screen with the camera restarted within 3 s and NO FRESH FRAMES until then; the first FIRE afterwards never lands on a stale frame.

R7.04.note: Mid-round: rotate the phone; no crash, no frozen crosshair, no hit from the pre-rotation frame.

R7.05.note: Ten minutes of play on the warmest phone: no crash, frame period (bench line / debug FPS) grows by less than 50%, screen stays on.

R7.06.note: Airplane mode for 30 s mid-round: aiming and verdicts continue locally, hits queue or fail visibly, the room resyncs with no duplicated hits.

R7.08.note: The demo runs from https://lazer-shooter-game.vercel.app with a real certificate (HTTP/2 200 over TLS on 2026-09-17), so no self-signed certificate is involved.

R7.09.note: First open on venue Wi-Fi: models downloaded and warmed up within 30 s with the status pill visible; second open instant (PWA cache); one phone reopened offline.

R7.10.note: Sounds and haptics on hit, being hit, elimination and win, audible in a noisy room; iOS after the first tap.

R7.12.note: 20-minute round on a midrange phone, torch off: battery drop under 25%.

R7.14.note: Add to home screen on iOS and Android; the installed app behaves like the tab.
